messages:
maria.devops: Heads up — customer P-772 asking how we should surface pass-through for on‑prem license + cloud egress when they run Private/VPC with reserved commit. They want an invoice that separates 'license' vs 'infrastructure' vs 'cloud egress'. Can we confirm what's allowed?

sam.finance: Short answer: we can pass through vendor invoices for cloud egress if the vendor provides a verifiable invoice or metering export. Third‑party license pass‑through only when it's in the contract. Reserved commit handling varies. Need to align w/ legal.

chris.infra: Quick infra note — for Private on customer HW we still record `gpu_hours` from the local agent. So per‑GPU-hour metering is possible if we agree on pricing table. But if they're using their own infra, we don't bill infra unless it's part of a managed offering.

lee.sales: Customer expects credit if they move committed capacity to on‑prem. Can we offer a transition credit or would finance reject? @sam.finance? :thinking_face:

anya.security: Also callout: KMS/HSM integrations and model license constraints. If customer uses their KMS, there may be an integration fee in the SOW. And some model weights have non‑commercial clauses — legal needs to confirm pass‑through/redistribution rights.

sam.finance: TL;DR: (1) Cloud egress = pass‑through if vendor invoice exists. (2) Vendor license fee = pass‑through only if contractually allowed. (3) Reserved commit refunds = default NO, but we can offer time‑limited credit or pro‑rata transfer in specific cases. I'll get legal involved on model license bits.

chris.infra: Example invoice lines I'll produce (sample):

```
Invoice 2026-0912
- Redwood platform fee (monthly): $12,000
- Reserved GPU commit (monthly pro‑rata): $8,400
- Vendor model license (pass‑through): $2,100
- Cloud egress (vendor pass‑through): $350
- KMS/HSM integration one‑time: $1,200
```

maria.devops: Customer asked if we can generate per-node/per‑GPU line items from our agent telemetry. We do have a `gpu_hours` export in the Private agent. Can that be turned into invoiceable rows?

billing-bot: /reports/P-772/2026-03-01_2026-03-31.csv generated and uploaded to s3://redwood-prod-reports/P-772/2026-03-31.csv (owner: chris.infra)

sam.finance: Yes — we can ingest that CSV and map to an "infrastructure usage" invoice section, as long as the contract includes per‑GPU pricing. If not, we need an addendum. Also ensure taxes/VAT handling for EU customers is accounted for on pass‑through lines.

lee.sales: :thumbsup: I'll propose a 3‑month transition credit to the customer while they migrate reserved capacity on‑prem. That should keep them happy. Will ask them to sign an addendum that permits vendor invoice passthrough and per‑GPU metering.

anya.security: One more flag — for third‑party model licenses run on customer on‑prem: some licenses forbid charging for access or packaging. Legal check required before we list it as a billable line.

sam.finance: Action items: @chris.infra create sample per‑node invoice CSV and share link (EOD). @lee.sales & @sam.finance draft addendum template for pass‑through + transition credit (48h). @anya.security send model license checklist to legal. I'll coordinate tax treatment.

chris.infra: On it — will attach the CSV to the finance drive and ping here when ready.
